cases.command: rm -f /data/pipe-produced; for i in {1..20}; do echo x >> /data/pipe-produced; echo "$i"; sleep 0.02; done | head -n 1; produced=$(wc -l < /data/pipe-produced); test "$produced" -ge 1 && test "$produced" -lt 20
set -o pipefail; for i in 1 2 3; do echo "$i"; done | head -n 1; echo "status=$? pipestatus=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"
set -o pipefail; for i in 1 2 3; do echo "$i"; sleep 0.05; done | head -n 1; echo "status=$? pipestatus=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"
rm -f /data/sub-count; echo pre$(echo x >> /data/sub-count; printf value)post; wc -l < /data/sub-count
rm -f /data/sub-count; echo {a,b}$(echo x >> /data/sub-count; printf value); wc -l < /data/sub-count

cases.note: The two-byte é begins at byte 16383 (zero based), across the 16 KiB boundary. Covers file and pipeline decoders.
cases.command: { printf '%16383s' '' | tr ' ' a; printf 'é'; printf '%16384s' '' | tr ' ' b; } > /data/chunk-utf8; wc -c < /data/chunk-utf8; wc -m < /data/chunk-utf8; cat /data/chunk-utf8 | wc -m; wc -w < /data/chunk-utf8; grep -bo 'aéb' /data/chunk-utf8; head -c 16385 /data/chunk-utf8 | wc -m; tail -c 16384 /data/chunk-utf8 | wc -c; rm /data/chunk-utf8

cases.note: A word spans byte 16384, with a final line lacking a newline.
cases.command: { printf '%16383s' ''; printf 'alpha beta\ngamma'; } > /data/chunk-words; wc -w < /data/chunk-words; wc -l < /data/chunk-words; wc -m < /data/chunk-words; grep -o 'alpha' /data/chunk-words; tail -n 1 /data/chunk-words; printf '\n'; rm /data/chunk-words

cases.note: 31-byte lines straddle the 16 KiB boundary; count and early-exit consumers read the same stream.
cases.command: for i in $(seq 1 700); do printf '012345678901234567890123456789\n'; done > /data/chunk-lines; wc -c < /data/chunk-lines; cat /data/chunk-lines | wc -l; grep -c '456789' /data/chunk-lines; head -n 529 /data/chunk-lines | wc -c; tail -n 172 /data/chunk-lines | wc -c; rm /data/chunk-lines

cases.note: Quiet search stops globally, while -m and -c remain per file.
cases.command:
mkdir -p /data/grep-stop/nested; printf 'hit
hit

hit
